I like the concept of this game. I really like [b]Bloodshed[/b] so I buy this game as soon as it came out. I am the target audience for this game. [b]I didn't like this game.[/b] The game has a decent weapon impact. That's where the positives end. The game is made in the [b]style medieval shooter[/b], like the Doom TDE, Witchfire, Painkiller well you get it. [b]I don't like it.[/b] There are no real guns, the guns are just dont look cool, I don't like the guns visually. In terms of style, the game tries to copy new Doom, but it looks much much worse. So the game has no own style and looks worse than the original it imitates. HELLBREAK currently has 2 tiny, symmetrical arenas. They are grim, unremarkable and get boring quickly. [b]AWFUL performance.[/b] The entire game takes place on a tiny arena with not that many enemies. At the same time, the game is very demanding on hardware. Visually, the game does not look beautiful, it looks bland, it looks worse than games from 10 years ago, but it works much worse! The worst thing you can expect from an Unreal Engine, enjoy the game with DLSS. Unfortunately, I do not recommend this game. There are plenty of other boomer shooters that are better now.

用了几个小时把所有难度都过了一遍，这款游戏玩起来还是比较爽的。尤其是后面怪非常多的时候，杀的挺解压的。用固定套路基本都可以通关 [spoiler] 游戏里面“虚弱”诅咒这个buff，在后面群怪聚集起来的时候清的还是比较快的，不会有太多瞄准上的压力。其次就是回血、免伤的法术或者祝福，刷出来都可以选，可以增加容错。武器方面，初始“女妖”升到满级，对于目前有的难度来说是够用的。“扭曲者”这把左轮我用的也比较多，单体爆头伤害不管对于小怪还是boss来说都很高，配上“虚弱”buff清小怪也很快。近战中期挺有用的，但后期有自爆，我就不怎么用了。对于手雷，个人倾向于分裂的虚弱雷，同理清怪快。预兆者短喷buff叠起来近距离伤害极高，配神盾和洗罪。撕裂者是最无脑清图的。 [/spoiler] 游戏玩下来个人觉得有几个特点和BUG。 随着游戏难度变高，怪非常多一局，基本上就是一直跑打。 怪聚集太多之后，用“虚弱”诅咒一次杀太多，游戏画面会卡顿。 其余也没什么了，期待后续更新

First, let me be clear: The game is incredibly fun. The combat is exhilarating and intense, and there’s a real satisfaction in tearing through hordes of demons. However, as a paying customer, if you were to ask me, "Do I recommend this game?" I’d have to hesitate. While the combat is great, the game suffers from several significant drawbacks. 1. Lack of Content There are only three maps in total. You’re essentially forced to play the same stages over and over again on increasing difficulty levels. While there are unlockables, the progression system is tedious; even though the maps are limited, you aren't given access to all difficulties at once. You have to grind each map from the easiest setting to the hardest one by one. 2. Shallow "Roguelite" Elements The game borrows a few Roguelite mechanics, but aside from picking random abilities upon leveling up, there’s nothing else there. It’s hard to even call it a "permadeath" game. It feels more like playing a series of standalone Slayer’s Gates from Doom Eternal. 3. Sluggish Pacing The game is painfully slow. There is no sprint mechanic. While there is a dash similar to Doom Eternal, the cooldown is agonizingly long, making it a "dodge-only" move rather than a traversal tool. Consequently, you spend most of your time walking slowly. Fighting weak zombies at a snail's pace every single round eventually becomes a chore. 4. Broken Weapon and Enemy Balance Weapon balance is all over the place—some are absurdly overpowered, while others are uselessly weak. Since you pick one weapon at the start, there’s no reason to ever choose a weaker one. Furthermore, certain late-game demons are extremely frustrating to deal with depending on your weapon type. The game offers no tactical workarounds for this, which feels unfair and forces you to stick to "all-rounder" weapons rather than experimenting with your preferences. 5. Constant Interruptions (Upgrade Overload) The game utilizes the common Roguelite mechanic of choosing one of three random upgrades upon leveling up. The problem is that it happens too often. Without exaggeration, you’ll be looking at the upgrade screen dozens of times in a single match. Every time you level up, the action stops completely. You have to read the text and consider your current build, which repeatedly breaks the flow of combat. 6. Poor Optimization The optimization is disappointing. Despite the textures appearing blurry and low-res, the frame rate tanks as soon as a few demons gather on screen. Using AoE (Area of Effect) skills or crowd control makes the performance drop even further. On a system with an RTX 4070 Ti and 128GB of DDR5 RAM, failing to maintain a stable 60 FPS is unacceptable. Conclusion The combat is fun, but the content is thin and the gameplay loop is sluggish. If you’re looking for the lightning-fast pacing of Doom Eternal, the slow movement will frustrate you. If you’re a fan of Roguelites, the shallow systems and poor balance will disappoint you. It’s an odd "mishmash" of genres that fails to fully satisfy either side. Given that these issues seem baked into the game's core design since early development, I doubt they will improve significantly over time. Only buy this if you are strictly looking for a game where you can rip and tear through demons to a heavy metal soundtrack. (Just to be clear: I personally had a lot of fun with this game)

For now, I recommend this game if you want to contribute to the making of a potential awesome game in the future so I'll still give this a positive review. Otherwise, there are other games right now you can try out.

WHAT A GREAT GAME! Heavily inspired by DOOM in all the right ways. FPS meets vampire survivors formula. Looks great Runs great (for me at least) Shooting is great and the guns are fun. Levels are well designed and have a great look to them. Progression is grindy but that's part of the appeal for this type of game 4 different levels. The maps expand as you survive. Which opens up new routes to kite enemies into or break lines of site. Weapons are mostly really enjoyable and pack a punch. They can be upgraded with xp and crystals dropped by defeating bosses. Skills are fun and synergize well. And you can get cards which combine two different effects such as "shock" and "inferno" create "plasma". Not a whole heck of alot of them but what's there is fun. Movement if fun. Dashing gives you i-frames. Plus you can get cards that attach damage to them. Such as dashing through enemies applies "blight" or "shock". Well done Devs! Hat's off to you gents. This has been a perfect game for me.

Hellbreak is basically mixing Doom and and vampire survivor-like games. If you just relax, run around an arena and shoot stuff this is the game for you. It's good and it's fun and I do recommend it. In terms of content, there seems to be a lot to do. Multiple maps/arenas and multiple difficulties with a perk tree and multiple loadouts. The progression is there and the ability to have some customisation in preparation for your runs is too which is really nice. The rest I do have some criticism for, there's a lot of quality of life to be done. It's a decent game that I have and will continue to enjoy playing, however it's definitely lacking in some areas: [list] [*]Movement - The movement to me felt a lot more slow and less fluid than I think is intended, jump pads felt awful to be on just because they slow you down so much, and there's no sense of momentum from dashes and jump pads whatsoever. Even with some movement speed options you're feeling a bit stuck and sluggish rather than dashing and jumping about and hopping about, which doesn't sound like much but it's a massive set back to the gameplay loop having the dashing and boost/jump pads and just them not providing any sense of momentum whatsoever. In this game I understand how too much fluidness and momentum would be overpowered but it creates a higher skill ceiling and the opportunity for even higher difficulties and challenges which overall results in a lot more fun and addictive gameplay loop. [*]Entry level difficulty - To me, the difficulty 1 and difficulty 2 options just felt really easy, and as a result it hasn't really got me hooked. So far the arena just feels like a half empty cakewalk and that's no fun to me. Hopefully will prove a challenge once I'm at difficulties 4 and 5. [*]More graphics options - Motion Blur and Bloom should be in the graphics options. Many many players including myself can't stand playing with these two in a game. Also there is a gamma option but it only turns it down when you increase the slider? If that's intentional I dislike the decision. I had a problem on the colosseum stage where the lighting made it so I couldn't see in certain areas due to how dark the shadows were. They didn't look like shadows, but just massive dark pitch black areas. (Graphics all on Epic and no performance issues.) [*]No colourblind or accessibility options - I can't tell if my spell's are on cooldown and I can't tell which spells I have equipped due to colour-blindness. Whilst not detrimental at the moment it is going to be once I'm at the higher difficulties. A colourblind option would be nice an easy fix for me would just be able to alter the colours like on other games. Again, motion blur toggle is also an accessibility option. [*]Basic crosshair customisation - It would be nice to have the ability to use the same crosshair across all weapons, or not display crosshair spread and bloom and things like that. [*] Run variety - The choices given on level ups so far are really cool, but there's so little! I got 3 runs in on my first session and throughout those runs I've seen all the same combinations come by (other than guns) and it's just going to start feeling the same choices and decisions over and over again. 4 Elements, same 2-3 upgrades but they apply a different element and basic stats. The armour does add a lot of variety to prepare for your runs, but during a run there isn't much. [/list] Overall the devs still have executed well on the doom inspired action roguelike. It just feels like there's still things missing to differentiate it from being a good game to being a staple addicting rogue like. Despite some criticism it's still a fun game to run around and shoot things. It achieves what it's aiming for but also a refreshing take on the genre too. Credit where credit is due too they've provided a better experience in the the action fps genre than that Painkiller reboot!

Game has a solid and promising feature judging by its current state. At the moment the game feels way too clunky and >ME< >PERSONALLY< will avoid it for now and wait for future updates with high hopes. Examples: 1. No real "feeling" when you damage an enemy, its like you are attacking bots that just don't care about the damage they receive (when they don't insta-die or get affected by ailments, of course) 2. Feedback of the damage received is almost non-existent, close to zero even. Enemies attack you and your character doesn't feel the damage received, he just keeps walking and you barely have an idea that you took damage. Which brings me to critic number 3. 3. UI needs a REWORK ASAP. I start the maps with 100% HP and out of nowhere I look at the HP bar, which is small as hell (average size in real life), and realize I have 10% left. Make it bigger or just remake the User UI entirely. Same goes for Spells/Abilities; I rarely know when they are up, 4. Some of the enemies are a little bit broken early game (personally don't care, but will add it anyway). Those were the bad, now the good: 1. TOP TIER MUSIC/SOUNDTRACK. 2. The weapon designs and their abilities are creative, fun and powerful as hell (you will realize for a random second or two that you have a little bit of damage feedback and then forget it again) 3. The Blessings/Skills you get are customizable with your playstyle and the current weapon, which makes it fun to try a few different combinations! 4. The spells are a cool way to add more "content" to the game, but I rarely remember using them aside from a few OP ones. But they are insanely fun to mess around at the start as well! 5. Passive tree is huge and it allows you to upgrade lots of stuff that will make the game WAY easier. Just will add that you can also upgrade the weapons, which is pretty cool. That's it for me. I really enjoy fast-paced roguelikes but this one isn't cooked yet IMO.

"This is Doom meets XYZ" is such a marketing-ploy at this point... For a small game it mimicks Doom well enough, but do not delude yourself or other players: This is most definitely not anywhere near Doom levels. It can be fun, but it very much depends on your RNG-luck and how far you've developed the guns....and which one you choose. You fight waves of enemies until you reach the 20 minute mark and "survive" the round. Maps are mostly boring, strangely vertical considering that jumping is sketchy and you can't grab plattforms to ascend. The jump pads in this game are by far the worst I've yet to see in an arena shooter - they will propell you in the same direction every time, as in their propulsion is fixed - it feels so odd when you backpaddel, run into a jump-pad and get thrown back in the direction you came from. Hitboxes are a bit messy, both in terms of enemies as well as the environemtn. It is rather easy to get stuck on geometry. Weapon sounds vary from pretty cool to wet fart - the later goes double for everything Shotgun (further prove that this is most definitely NOT Doom....) Enemies are ripped pretty much straight out of Doom I and behave as dumb as them. They mindlessly walk, run, fly (dear lord, the flying enemies in this game...) or jump towards you and will struggle to walk around pillars and such. Most projectile-based enemies, though, have impeccable aim and path-calculation. Weapon and Curse balancing is completely off the scale. I found that the Shredder and the Shellshock are just broken, especially if comboed along with some blight curse. When you get this, the game actually gets crazy fun, because you just pop that blight all over the map. Inferno, for example, is dreadful. Shock works so-so and frost is very situational. If it is a random proc, it's useful, if you try to trigger it yourself, it's annoying. Other Weapons like the Minigun, the throwing dart - totally a Doom-staple - and some others are borderline useless for a variety of reasons. Minigun just doesn't have the ammo-count, dart is just way too imprecise, pistols are jokes and even the shotguns - apart from aforementioned shellshock, which is dumb-broken (effective range of a rifle, but still spreads like a shotgun, regenerates health upon kill, which is basically every shot that you don't miss) - are not fun. All weapons shine or fail not because of damage, ranges or things like that: It basically comes down to the reload-animation and the ammo count per magazine. If a gun has low ammo-count, it's a problem, because they all basically do the same damage. If it's topped of with slow reload, it's renedered useless. The game has a couple of those. Then you have guns like the shredder, which makes you not even have to aim and on ascended levels one shot will clear rooms full of enemies, because the saw-blade keeps spinning to the next enemy. You can have fun with this game, most definitely, but all in all, the thing that makes or breaks this type of simple game is the guns - unfortunately, they don't feel fleshed out enough. You don't want to try them out, because you pretty soon realize, which ones work and which ones don't. At that point, difficulty also gets pretty much negated, just because of how powerful certain combinations are. I went an hour on endless mode and only died because I stopped moving - still took me roughly 20 seconds, because I spammed so many AOE-traps every 2 seconds. I'll go ahead and grind me some more achievements out of this. Wanna-be Doom aesthetics and feel meets vampire survivor. Could be way better with some tweaks!
